summary: Reproduced that unresolved decode-side DP-rank lookups can be issued once per scheduler cycle even though current main already batches rooms and pools HTTP sessions. Added a per-bootstrap-address 10 ms rate limit shared by asynchronous prefetch and synchronous fallback, with cleanup when an address becomes inactive.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before regression: the real unresolved queue path queried on all 3 scheduler cycles instead of 2 interval-permitted attempts, and the independent-address throttle helper did not exist. Raw output: reports/j-ef41d35bf892/raw/failing-before.txt

Passing-after registered disaggregation suite: 360 passed and 45 subtests passed, including scheduler prefetch throttling, immediate first lookup, retry after the interval, and independent bootstrap-address behavior. Raw output: reports/j-ef41d35bf892/raw/disaggregation-unit-suite-passing.txt

gpu_execution_evidence: Inventory only: prepared Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2 saw one AMD Instinct MI350X with gcn_arch_name gfx950:sramecc+:xnack-. No GPU kernel or model serving execution was used for this CPU-side HTTP scheduling fix. Raw output: reports/j-ef41d35bf892/raw/gpu-inventory.txt
remaining_limitations: Only one gfx950 GPU and one node were assigned; the reported two-node TP8/EP8/DP8 MoRI topology could not be run.
The exact [Errno 99] ephemeral-port exhaustion was not reproduced; the deterministic regression proves the scheduler-cycle query flood that can drive it.
An independently unreachable bootstrap remains unreachable; this correction bounds query frequency but does not repair network reachability.
The prepared interpreter does not include the ruff module; git diff --check and the complete registered disaggregation unit suite were used instead.
